Wiikwemkoong Unceded Territory

Wiikwemkoong’s public history places its community on Odawa Mnis, or Manitoulin Island, within Three Fires relationships. A speaker’s dictionary account offers a second, locally situated route into language work.

01

Diplomacy, migration and community history

Wiikwemkoong’s historical account describes Odawa life on Manitoulin Island, relations among the Odawa, Ojibway and Potawatomi, and diplomacy with French and British newcomers. It records Wiikwemkoong’s refusal to sign the 1862 Manitoulin treaty and the 1968 amalgamation of the Manitoulin Island Unceded, Point Grondine and South Bay bands. These events are presented through the Nation’s account of its political history.

Read the sources [1] Wiikwemkoong Unceded Territory

02

A Wiikwemkoong speaker’s dictionary work

Mary Ann Corbiere explains that her way of speaking reflects Wiikwemkoong. Teaching prompted her to gather words absent from available dictionaries for an Odawa and Eastern Ojibwe project. Repeated workshops checked usage and generated further vocabulary; she also identifies limits where new entries could not be checked with every group. Her account treats documentation as continuing collaboration and judgment.

Read the sources [2] Proceedings of the 27th Stabilizing Indigenous Languages Symposium; Queen’s University journal platform

Gaa-Bizhiwebak — Our History ↗

The Nation’s public historical narrative connects Great Lakes diplomacy, nineteenth-century treaty pressures, amalgamation and language work. Treaty interpretations remain attributed to this account.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual history body, paragraphs from Odawa Mnis and early contact through the 1968 amalgamation, 2014 constitution and 2006 language strategy (web lines 146–169).

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Ngii-mchwe-mkoshin: One Speaker’s Experiences in Compiling a Dictionary by Trial and Error ↗

Publication: 2026-05-13

Mary Ann Corbiere situates dictionary work in her Wiikwemkoong speech and teaching experience. Repeated speaker checking expands the material while exposing limits in community attribution.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Fresh actual PDF reading of printed 105–109 (PDF pages 2–6): introduction, Wiikwemkoong speech context, teaching motivation and repeated checking workshops. Official landing page inspected for release date.
